card_quote: I want the surprising story behind the fact, not just the fact. I've little reading time and I dislike repetition and padding.
how_read: On the commute, a story or two each way, in order. Rounds 1 to 5 went quickly across the first week or so. Then physics in Round 6 felt heavier and I parked it on the bedside table. Not abandoned, just stalled, and it's the sort of book that is easy to pick up again.

w1_review.headline: Good commute fodder, but the same shape every page
w1_review.body: Short stories I can read in one stop and a handful that I passed on in the group chat. The odd thing is how similar the pages are: popular version, record, why it spread, repeat. Some stories come in pairs and the second one felt like padding. Bottom line: a good dip-in book for fact-podcast people and a decent gift for one, if you can live with the repetition.

w2_review_first: It's a nice dip-in book, a few really good surprising stories and a lot of the same structure. I'd say read ten, put it down, pick it up again later.

w2_lost.why: Napoleon straight after Hanlon, I felt I was reading the page twice.
Yerkes-Dodson and the mice, a lot of detail for something I didn't care about.
Laffer and the napkin, US politics, I drifted.

w2_cut.why: Disputed and second-hand, no story at the end.

w2_book2: If it's the same formula in every entry with no variety, or if the next one leans on US stories I've never heard of.
